$$\text{Work in 2-hour cycle} = 5 + 3 = 8\text{ units}$$
$$\text{In 3 cycles (6 hours), work done} = 3 \times 8 = 24\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 30 - 24 = 6\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Hour 7: A does } 5\text{ units. Remaining} = 1\text{ unit}$$
$$\text{Hour 8: B takes } \frac{1}{3}\text{ hour}$$
$$\text{Total time} = 6 + 1 + \frac{1}{3} = 7\frac{1}{3}\text{ hours}$$

typeHeader: TYPE - III: CONCEPT OF ALTERNATE DAYS
questionText: Avi and Bindu can complete a project in 4 and 12 hours, respectively. Avi begins project at 5 a.m., and they work alternately for one hour each. When will the project be completed?
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(4, 12) = 12\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of Avi} = 3,\quad \text{Efficiency of Bindu} = 1$$
$$\text{Work in 2-hour cycle} = 3 + 1 = 4\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Number of cycles} = \frac{12}{4} = 3\text{ cycles}$$
$$\text{Total hours taken} = 3 \times 2 = 6\text{ hours}$$
$$\text{Completion time} = 5\text{ a.m.} + 6\text{ hours} = 11\text{ a.m.}$$

typeHeader: TYPE - III: CONCEPT OF ALTERNATE DAYS
questionText: A man takes 16 days to complete a project. A woman does the same work in 12 days. They started the work together on alternate days and the man worked on the first day. How much time will they take to complete the work?
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(16, 12) = 48\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of Man} = 3,\quad \text{Efficiency of Woman} = 4$$
$$\text{Work in 2-day cycle} = 3 + 4 = 7\text{ units}$$
$$\text{In 6 cycles (12 days), work done} = 6 \times 7 = 42\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 48 - 42 = 6\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Day 13: Man works and does } 3\text{ units. Remaining} = 3\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Day 14: Woman works and takes } \frac{3}{4}\text{ day}$$
$$\text{Total time} = 12 + 1 + \frac{3}{4} = 13\frac{3}{4} = \frac{55}{4}\text{ days}$$

typeHeader: TYPE - III: CONCEPT OF ALTERNATE DAYS
questionText: A, B and C can complete a work in 10, 15 and 20 days, respectively. They work on alternate days such that 1st day A, 2nd day B and 3rd day C. Again 4th day A, 5th day B and so on. If they work in the same way, in how many days will the work be completed?
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(10, 15, 20) = 60\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of A} = 6,\quad \text{Efficiency of B} = 4,\quad \text{Efficiency of C} = 3$$
$$\text{Work in 3-day cycle} = 6 + 4 + 3 = 13\text{ units}$$
$$\text{In 4 cycles (12 days), work done} = 4 \times 13 = 52\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 60 - 52 = 8\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Day 13: A does } 6\text{ units. Remaining} = 2\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Day 14: B takes } \frac{2}{4} = \frac{1}{2}\text{ day}$$
$$\text{Total time} = 12 + 1 + \frac{1}{2} = 13\frac{1}{2}\text{ days}$$

typeHeader: TYPE - III: CONCEPT OF ALTERNATE DAYS
questionText: If Mohit, Nitu and Soma can complete a piece of work in 5 days, 6 days and 8 days, respectively, then in how many days will the work be completed if they work on alternate days starting with Mohit on first day, then Nitu on second day, then Soma on third day, then Mohit on fourth day and so on.
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(5, 6, 8) = 120\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of Mohit} = 24,\quad \text{Efficiency of Nitu} = 20,\quad \text{Efficiency of Soma} = 15$$
$$\text{Work in 3-day cycle} = 24 + 20 + 15 = 59\text{ units}$$
$$\text{In 2 cycles (6 days), work done} = 2 \times 59 = 118\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 120 - 118 = 2\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Day 7: Mohit takes } \frac{2}{24} = \frac{1}{12}\text{ day}$$
$$\text{Total time} = 6 + \frac{1}{12} = 6\frac{1}{12}\text{ days}$$

typeHeader: TYPE - III: CONCEPT OF ALTERNATE DAYS
questionText: A, B and C can separately complete a work in 20, 25 and 30 days, respectively. If A works on the first day alone, B on second day alone and C on the third day alone, and this sequence goes on further, in how many days will the entire work be finished?
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(20, 25, 30) = 300\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of A} = 15,\quad \text{Efficiency of B} = 12,\quad \text{Efficiency of C} = 10$$
$$\text{Work in 3-day cycle} = 15 + 12 + 10 = 37\text{ units}$$
$$\text{In 8 cycles (24 days), work done} = 8 \times 37 = 296\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 300 - 296 = 4\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Day 25: A takes } \frac{4}{15}\text{ day}$$
$$\text{Total time} = 24 + \frac{4}{15} = 24\frac{4}{15}\text{ days}$$

typeHeader: TYPE - III: CONCEPT OF ALTERNATE DAYS
questionText: Tushar, Megha, Punam and Richa can complete a piece of work in 10 days, 12 days, 15 days and 18 days, respectively. In how many days will the work be completed if each of them work on alternate days starting with Megha on first day, Punam on second day, Richa on third day, Tushar on fourth day and then again Megha on fifth day and so on.
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(10, 12, 15, 18) = 180\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Eff}(\text{Megha}) = 15,\quad \text{Eff}(\text{Punam}) = 12,\quad \text{Eff}(\text{Richa}) = 10,\quad \text{Eff}(\text{Tushar}) = 18$$
$$\text{Order: Megha, Punam, Richa, Tushar}$$
$$\text{Work in 4-day cycle} = 15 + 12 + 10 + 18 = 55\text{ units}$$
$$\text{In 3 cycles (12 days), work done} = 3 \times 55 = 165\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 180 - 165 = 15\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Day 13: Megha finishes } 15\text{ units in exactly } 1\text{ day}$$
$$\text{Total time} = 12 + 1 = 13\text{ days}$$

typeHeader: TYPE - III: CONCEPT OF ALTERNATE DAYS
questionText: A can do a piece of work in 24 days and B can do it in 80 days. B works alone for 2 days and A works alone on the 3rd day. This process continues till the work is completed. In how many days will the work be completed?
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(24, 80) = 240\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of A} = 10,\quad \text{Efficiency of B} = 3$$
$$\text{Work in 3-day cycle (B, B, A)} = 3 + 3 + 10 = 16\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Number of cycles} = \frac{240}{16} = 15\text{ cycles}$$
$$\text{Total time} = 15 \times 3 = 45\text{ days}$$

typeHeader: TYPE - III: CONCEPT OF ALTERNATE DAYS
questionText: A can complete a piece of work alone in 200 days, while B can complete the same piece of work alone in 100 days. In every three-day cycle, both A and B work on day 1, only A works on day 2, and only B works on day 3. This cycle continues till the work is completed. How many days in all does it take the duo to complete the work?
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(200, 100) = 200\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of A} = 1,\quad \text{Efficiency of B} = 2$$
$$\text{Day 1 (A + B)} = 3,\quad \text{Day 2 (A)} = 1,\quad \text{Day 3 (B)} = 2$$
$$\text{Work in 3-day cycle} = 3 + 1 + 2 = 6\text{ units}$$
$$\text{In 33 cycles (99 days), work done} = 33 \times 6 = 198\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 200 - 198 = 2\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Day 100: (A + B) work together and take } \frac{2}{3}\text{ day}$$
$$\text{Total time} = 99 + \frac{2}{3} = 99\frac{2}{3}\text{ days}$$

typeHeader: TYPE - III: CONCEPT OF ALTERNATE DAYS
questionText: P, Q and R can do a piece of work in 20 days, 30 days and 60 days respectively. If P works daily and on every third day Q and R also work with P, then in how many days, will the work be completed?
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(20, 30, 60) = 60\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of P} = 3,\quad \text{Efficiency of Q} = 2,\quad \text{Efficiency of R} = 1$$
$$\text{Day 1 (P)} = 3,\quad \text{Day 2 (P)} = 3,\quad \text{Day 3 (P + Q + R)} = 6$$
$$\text{Work in 3-day cycle} = 3 + 3 + 6 = 12\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Number of cycles} = \frac{60}{12} = 5\text{ cycles}$$
$$\text{Total days} = 5 \times 3 = 15\text{ days}$$

typeHeader: TYPE - III: CONCEPT OF ALTERNATE DAYS
questionText: A, B and C can do a piece of work in 11 days, 20 days and 55 days respectively. How soon can the work be done if A works with B on first day, A works with C on second day and so on?
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(11, 20, 55) = 220\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of A} = 20,\quad \text{Efficiency of B} = 11,\quad \text{Efficiency of C} = 4$$
$$\text{Day 1 (A + B)} = 20 + 11 = 31\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Day 2 (A + C)} = 20 + 4 = 24\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Work in 2-day cycle} = 31 + 24 = 55\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Number of cycles} = \frac{220}{55} = 4\text{ cycles}$$
$$\text{Total days} = 4 \times 2 = 8\text{ days}$$

typeHeader: TYPE - III: CONCEPT OF ALTERNATE DAYS
questionText: X, Y and Z can complete a work in 5 days, 15 days and 30 days, respectively. In how many days can the work be completed if X is assisted by Y and Z together, on every second day?
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(5, 15, 30) = 30\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of X} = 6,\quad \text{Efficiency of Y} = 2,\quad \text{Efficiency of Z} = 1$$
$$\text{Day 1 (X alone)} = 6\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Day 2 (X + Y + Z)} = 6 + 2 + 1 = 9\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Work in 2-day cycle} = 6 + 9 = 15\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Number of cycles} = \frac{30}{15} = 2\text{ cycles}$$
$$\text{Total days} = 2 \times 2 = 4\text{ days}$$

typeHeader: TYPE - III: CONCEPT OF ALTERNATE DAYS
questionText: P, Q and R can finish a work in 5 days, 10 days, and 15 days, respectively, working alone. P and Q works on first day, P and R works on second day and P and Q works on third day and so on till the work is completed. In how many days the work will be completed?
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(5, 10, 15) = 30\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of P} = 6,\quad \text{Efficiency of Q} = 3,\quad \text{Efficiency of R} = 2$$
$$\text{Day 1 (P + Q)} = 6 + 3 = 9\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Day 2 (P + R)} = 6 + 2 = 8\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Work in 2-day cycle} = 9 + 8 = 17\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work after 2 days} = 30 - 17 = 13\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Day 3 (P + Q)} = 9\text{ units. Remaining} = 13 - 9 = 4\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Day 4 (P + R)} = \frac{4}{8} = \frac{1}{2}\text{ day}$$
$$\text{Total time} = 2 + 1 + \frac{1}{2} = \frac{7}{2}\text{ days}$$

typeHeader: TYPE - III: CONCEPT OF ALTERNATE DAYS
questionText: A, B and C can complete a piece of work separately in 10, 20 and 40 days, respectively. In how many days will the work be completed if A is assisted by both B and C every third day?
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(10, 20, 40) = 40\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of A} = 4,\quad \text{Efficiency of B} = 2,\quad \text{Efficiency of C} = 1$$
$$\text{Day 1 (A)} = 4,\quad \text{Day 2 (A)} = 4,\quad \text{Day 3 (A + B + C)} = 4 + 2 + 1 = 7$$
$$\text{Work in 3-day cycle} = 4 + 4 + 7 = 15\text{ units}$$
$$\text{In 2 cycles (6 days), work done} = 2 \times 15 = 30\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 40 - 30 = 10\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Day 7: A does } 4\text{ units. Remaining} = 6\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Day 8: A does } 4\text{ units. Remaining} = 2\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Day 9: (A + B + C) take } \frac{2}{7}\text{ day}$$
$$\text{Total time} = 6 + 2 + \frac{2}{7} = 8\frac{2}{7}\text{ days}$$

typeHeader: TYPE - III: CONCEPT OF ALTERNATE DAYS
questionText: Ruchi, Khushi and Teju can do a piece of work in 30, 40 and 60 days respectively. In how many days can Ruchi do the work, if she is assisted by both Khushi and Teju on every third day?
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(30, 40, 60) = 120\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of Ruchi} = 4,\quad \text{Efficiency of Khushi} = 3,\quad \text{Efficiency of Teju} = 2$$
$$\text{Day 1 (Ruchi)} = 4,\quad \text{Day 2 (Ruchi)} = 4,\quad \text{Day 3 (All three)} = 9$$
$$\text{Work in 3-day cycle} = 4 + 4 + 9 = 17\text{ units}$$
$$\text{In 7 cycles (21 days), work done} = 7 \times 17 = 119\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 120 - 119 = 1\text{ unit}$$
$$\text{Day 22: Ruchi takes } \frac{1}{4}\text{ day}$$
$$\text{Total time} = 21 + \frac{1}{4} = \frac{85}{4}\text{ days}$$

typeHeader: TYPE - III: CONCEPT OF ALTERNATE DAYS
questionText: A, B and C can do a piece of work in 11 days, 20 days and 55 days respectively. If B works daily and is supported by A and C on alternate days beginning with A, then in how many days will the work be finished?
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(11, 20, 55) = 220\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of A} = 20,\quad \text{Efficiency of B} = 11,\quad \text{Efficiency of C} = 4$$
$$\text{Day 1 (B + A)} = 11 + 20 = 31\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Day 2 (B + C)} = 11 + 4 = 15\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Work in 2-day cycle} = 31 + 15 = 46\text{ units}$$
$$\text{In 4 cycles (8 days), work done} = 4 \times 46 = 184\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 220 - 184 = 36\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Day 9 (B + A)} = 31\text{ units. Remaining} = 5\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Day 10 (B + C)} = \frac{5}{15} = \frac{1}{3}\text{ day}$$
$$\text{Total time} = 8 + 1 + \frac{1}{3} = 9\frac{1}{3}\text{ days}$$

typeHeader: TYPE - III: CONCEPT OF ALTERNATE DAYS
questionText:
A alone can do a work in 11 days. B alone can do the same work in 22 days. C alone can do the same work in 33 days. They work in the following manner:
Day 1: A and B work.
Day 2: B and C work.
Day 3: C and A work.
Day 4: A and B work.
In how many days will the work be completed?
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(11, 22, 33) = 66\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of A} = 6,\quad \text{Efficiency of B} = 3,\quad \text{Efficiency of C} = 2$$
$$\text{Day 1 (A + B)} = 6 + 3 = 9\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Day 2 (B + C)} = 3 + 2 = 5\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Day 3 (C + A)} = 2 + 6 = 8\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Work in 3-day cycle} = 9 + 5 + 8 = 22\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Number of cycles} = \frac{66}{22} = 3\text{ cycles}$$
$$\text{Total time} = 3 \times 3 = 9\text{ days}$$

typeHeader: TYPE - III: CONCEPT OF ALTERNATE DAYS
questionText: A and B complete a work in 24 and 30 days, respectively, working 10 hours per day. The work is to be done in two shifts. The morning shift is for 6 hours and the evening shift is for 4 hours. On the first day, A works in the morning and B works in the evening, and they interchange their shifts every day. On which day did the work get completed?
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(240, 300) = 1200\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Hourly efficiency of A} = 5,\quad \text{Hourly efficiency of B} = 4$$
$$\text{Odd days (A in morning 6h, B in evening 4h)} = (6 \times 5) + (4 \times 4) = 46\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Even days (B in morning 6h, A in evening 4h)} = (6 \times 4) + (4 \times 5) = 44\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Work in 2-day cycle} = 46 + 44 = 90\text{ units}$$
$$\text{In 13 cycles (26 days), work done} = 13 \times 90 = 1170\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 1200 - 1170 = 30\text{ units}$$
$$\text{On Day 27 (morning shift), A works 6h and does } 6 \times 5 = 30\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Thus, the work is completed on the 27th day.}$$

typeHeader: TYPE - III: CONCEPT OF ALTERNATE DAYS
questionText: R, S and T can finish a work in 20, 15 and 10 days, respectively, R works on all days and S and T work on alternate days with T starting the work on the first day. In how many days is the work finished?
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(20, 15, 10) = 60\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of R} = 3,\quad \text{Efficiency of S} = 4,\quad \text{Efficiency of T} = 6$$
$$\text{Day 1 (R + T)} = 3 + 6 = 9\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Day 2 (R + S)} = 3 + 4 = 7\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Work in 2-day cycle} = 9 + 7 = 16\text{ units}$$
$$\text{In 3 cycles (6 days), work done} = 3 \times 16 = 48\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 60 - 48 = 12\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Day 7 (R + T)} = 9\text{ units. Remaining} = 3\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Day 8 (R + S)} = \frac{3}{7}\text{ day}$$
$$\text{Total time} = 6 + 1 + \frac{3}{7} = \frac{52}{7}\text{ days}$$

typeHeader: TYPE - III: CONCEPT OF ALTERNATE DAYS
questionText: A and B are equally efficient, and each can individually complete a piece of work in 36 days, if none takes any holiday. A and B started working together on this piece of work, but A took a day off after every five days of work, while B took a day off after every seven days of work. If they had started work on 1 July 2021, on which date was the work completed?
solution:
$$\text{Let efficiency of each be } 1\text{ unit/day. Total work} = 36\text{ units.}$$
$$\text{A rests on days: 6, 12, 18, 24...}$$
$$\text{B rests on days: 8, 16, 24...}$$
$$\text{Daily work tracking:}$$
$$\text{Days 1 to 5: both work } \implies 5 \times 2 = 10\text{ units (cum. 10)}$$
$$\text{Day 6: A rests, B works } \implies 1\text{ unit (cum. 11)}$$
$$\text{Day 7: both work } \implies 2\text{ units (cum. 13)}$$
$$\text{Day 8: A works, B rests } \implies 1\text{ unit (cum. 14)}$$
$$\text{Days 9 to 11: both work } \implies 3 \times 2 = 6\text{ units (cum. 20)}$$
$$\text{Day 12: A rests, B works } \implies 1\text{ unit (cum. 21)}$$
$$\text{Days 13 to 15: both work } \implies 3 \times 2 = 6\text{ units (cum. 27)}$$
$$\text{Day 16: A works, B rests } \implies 1\text{ unit (cum. 28)}$$
$$\text{Day 17: both work } \implies 2\text{ units (cum. 30)}$$
$$\text{Day 18: A rests, B works } \implies 1\text{ unit (cum. 31)}$$
$$\text{Days 19 and 20: both work } \implies 2 \times 2 = 4\text{ units (cum. 35)}$$
$$\text{Day 21: both work, needing only } 1\text{ unit to reach 36 units.}$$
$$\text{Thus, the work is completed on Day 21, i.e., 21 July 2021.}$$

typeHeader: TYPE - III: CONCEPT OF ALTERNATE DAYS
questionText: A and B are equally efficient, and each could individually complete a piece of work in 30 days, if none took any holiday. A and B started working together on this piece of work, but A took a day off after every four days of work, while B took a day off after every five days of work. If the duo had started work on 01 August 2022, on which date was the work completed?
solution:
$$\text{Let efficiency of each be } 1\text{ unit/day. Total work} = 30\text{ units.}$$
$$\text{A rests on days: 5, 10, 15, 20...}$$
$$\text{B rests on days: 6, 12, 18, 24...}$$
$$\text{Daily tracking:}$$
$$\text{Days 1 to 4: both work } \implies 4 \times 2 = 8\text{ units (cum. 8)}$$
$$\text{Day 5: A rests, B works } \implies 1\text{ unit (cum. 9)}$$
$$\text{Day 6: A works, B rests } \implies 1\text{ unit (cum. 10)}$$
$$\text{Days 7 to 9: both work } \implies 3 \times 2 = 6\text{ units (cum. 16)}$$
$$\text{Day 10: A rests, B works } \implies 1\text{ unit (cum. 17)}$$
$$\text{Day 11: both work } \implies 2\text{ units (cum. 19)}$$
$$\text{Day 12: A works, B rests } \implies 1\text{ unit (cum. 20)}$$
$$\text{Days 13 to 14: both work } \implies 2 \times 2 = 4\text{ units (cum. 24)}$$
$$\text{Day 15: A rests, B works } \implies 1\text{ unit (cum. 25)}$$
$$\text{Days 16 to 17: both work } \implies 2 \times 2 = 4\text{ units (cum. 29)}$$
$$\text{Day 18: A works (B rests), doing the 30th unit.}$$
$$\text{Thus, the work was completed on Day 18, i.e., 18 August 2022.}$$

typeHeader: TYPE - III: CONCEPT OF ALTERNATE DAYS
questionText: Two men A and B, each working alone by working 12 hours per day, can complete a work in 20 days. For execution of the work, it was decided that A and B would be working for 8 and 6 hours per day, respectively, on alternate days starting with A. If it takes x days and y hours to complete the work then (x, y) is:
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = 20 \times 12 = 240\text{ man-hours}$$
$$\text{Day 1 (A): } 8\text{ hours},\quad \text{Day 2 (B): } 6\text{ hours}$$
$$\text{Work in 2-day cycle} = 8 + 6 = 14\text{ hours}$$
$$\text{In 17 cycles (34 days), work done} = 17 \times 14 = 238\text{ hours}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 240 - 238 = 2\text{ hours}$$
$$\text{On Day 35, A works for 2 hours to complete the remaining work.}$$
$$\text{Hence, } x = 34\text{ full days and } y = 2\text{ hours} \implies (x, y) = (34, 2)$$

typeHeader: TYPE - III: CONCEPT OF ALTERNATE DAYS
questionText: Ratnesh and Vineet worked on alternate days, starting with Ratnesh. The entire work got completed in $54\frac{3}{4}$ days. If Ratnesh alone can finish the work in 48 days, then in how many days can Vineet alone do the work?
solution:
$$\text{Total time} = 54\frac{3}{4}\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Starting with Ratnesh: Ratnesh worked on odd days (27 full days } + \frac{3}{4}\text{ day}) = \frac{111}{4}\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Vineet worked on even days (27 full days)}$$
$$\text{Daily rate of Ratnesh} = \frac{1}{48}$$
$$\text{Work done by Ratnesh} = \frac{111}{4} \times \frac{1}{48} = \frac{37}{64}$$
$$\text{Work done by Vineet} = 1 - \frac{37}{64} = \frac{27}{64}$$
$$\text{Daily rate of Vineet} = \frac{27/64}{27} = \frac{1}{64}$$
$$\text{Time taken by Vineet alone} = 64\text{ days}$$

typeHeader: TYPE - III: CONCEPT OF ALTERNATE DAYS
questionText: A man and woman working on alternate days can finish a work in 15 days if the man works on the first day. The same work is finished in 14.5 days if they work on alternate days and if the woman starts on the first day. The work will be finished by a man alone in ______ days.
solution:
$$\text{Case 1 (Man starts, 15 days): Man works 8 days, Woman works 7 days: } W = 8M + 7W$$
$$\text{Case 2 (Woman starts, 14.5 days): Woman works 7.5 days, Man works 7 days: } W = 7M + 7.5W$$
$$8M + 7W = 7M + 7.5W \implies M = 0.5W \implies W = 2M$$
$$\text{Total work } W = 8M + 7(2M) = 22M$$
$$\text{Time taken by a man alone} = 22\text{ days}$$

typeHeader: TYPE - III: CONCEPT OF ALTERNATE DAYS
questionText: To do a certain work, Ajay and Bharat work on alternate days, with Bharat starting the work on the first day. Ajay can finish the work alone in 32 days. If the work gets completed in exactly 8 days, then Bharat alone can finish 7 times the same work in _____ days.
solution:
$$\text{In 8 days with Bharat starting, Bharat works 4 days and Ajay works 4 days.}$$
$$\text{Work done by Ajay in 4 days} = \frac{4}{32} = \frac{1}{8}$$
$$\text{Work done by Bharat in 4 days} = 1 - \frac{1}{8} = \frac{7}{8}$$
$$\text{Rate of Bharat} = \frac{7/8}{4} = \frac{7}{32}\text{ work/day}$$
$$\text{Time for Bharat to complete 7 times the work} = \frac{7}{7/32} = 32\text{ days}$$

typeHeader: TYPE - III: CONCEPT OF ALTERNATE DAYS
questionText: To do a certain work, A and B work on alternate days with B beginning the work on the first day. A alone can complete the same work in 24 days. If the work gets completed in $11\frac{1}{3}$ days, then B alone can complete $\frac{7}{9}$ part of the original work in:
solution:
$$\text{In } 11\frac{1}{3}\text{ days with B starting:}$$
$$\text{B works on days 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 (6 full days)}$$
$$\text{A works on days 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 (5 days) } + \frac{1}{3}\text{ of day 12} = \frac{16}{3}\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Work done by A} = \frac{16}{3} \times \frac{1}{24} = \frac{2}{9}$$
$$\text{Work done by B in 6 days} = 1 - \frac{2}{9} = \frac{7}{9}$$
$$\text{Hence, B alone completes } \frac{7}{9}\text{ of the original work in } 6\text{ days.}$$

typeHeader: TYPE - III: CONCEPT OF ALTERNATE DAYS
questionText: Aman and Rajan are working at a construction site. In some engineering experiment, Aman is constructing a wall, while Rajan is demolishing that wall. Aman can completely build the wall in 15 days, while Rajan will take 20 days to completely demolish the wall. In how many days will the complete wall be built for the first time if they work on alternate days, with Aman working on the 1st day?
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(15, 20) = 60\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of Aman (building)} = +4\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of Rajan (demolishing)} = -3\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Net work in 2-day cycle} = +4 - 3 = +1\text{ unit}$$
$$\text{Target before final building day} = 60 - 4 = 56\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Days to reach 56 units} = 56 \times 2 = 112\text{ days}$$
$$\text{On Day 113, Aman builds 4 units: total reaches } 56 + 4 = 60\text{ units (completely built).}$$
$$\text{Total days} = 113\text{ days}$$

typeHeader: TYPE - III: CONCEPT OF ALTERNATE DAYS
questionText: A can do a piece of work in 36 days, while B can do it in 48 days. B worked on it for 12 days and leaves it. How many days will A take to finish the remaining work?
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(36, 48) = 144\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of A} = 4,\quad \text{Efficiency of B} = 3$$
$$\text{Work done by B in 12 days} = 12 \times 3 = 36\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 144 - 36 = 108\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by A alone} = \frac{108}{4} = 27\text{ days}$$

typeHeader: TYPE - IV: CONCEPT OF LEAVING THE WORK
questionText: A can do a piece of work in 10 days and B can do it in 15 days. They work together for 2 days and then A leaves. How long will B take to finish the remaining work?
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(10, 15) = 30\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of A} = 3,\quad \text{Efficiency of B} = 2$$
$$\text{Work done by (A + B) in 2 days} = 2 \times (3 + 2) = 10\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 30 - 10 = 20\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by B alone} = \frac{20}{2} = 10\text{ days}$$

typeHeader: TYPE - IV: CONCEPT OF LEAVING THE WORK
questionText: P and Q can do a work together in 30 days. Q and R can do the same work together in 24 days and R and P together in 20 days. They started the work together, but Q and R left after 10 days. How many more days will P take to finish the remaining work?
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(30, 24, 20) = 120\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Eff}(P + Q) = 4,\quad \text{Eff}(Q + R) = 5,\quad \text{Eff}(R + P) = 6$$
$$2 \times \text{Eff}(P + Q + R) = 15 \implies \text{Eff}(P + Q + R) = 7.5\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of P} = 7.5 - 5 = 2.5\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Work done by all three in 10 days} = 10 \times 7.5 = 75\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 120 - 75 = 45\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by P alone} = \frac{45}{2.5} = 18\text{ days}$$

typeHeader: TYPE - IV: CONCEPT OF LEAVING THE WORK
questionText: Rohan alone can complete a work in 12 days and Hari alone can complete it in 16 days. They both work for 3 days and then Rohan leaves the work. After that Hari works alone and completes the work. In how many days will the total work be completed?
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(12, 16) = 48\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of Rohan} = 4,\quad \text{Efficiency of Hari} = 3$$
$$\text{Work done by both in 3 days} = 3 \times (4 + 3) = 21\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 48 - 21 = 27\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by Hari alone} = \frac{27}{3} = 9\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Total days for work completion} = 3 + 9 = 12\text{ days}$$

typeHeader: TYPE - IV: CONCEPT OF LEAVING THE WORK
questionText: P can do a piece of work in 30 days and Q in 40 days. They work together for 4 days and then Q leaves. The number of days taken by P to finish the remaining work is:

$$\text{Remaining work} = 120 - 28 = 92\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by P alone} = \frac{92}{4} = 23\text{ days}$$

typeHeader: TYPE - IV: CONCEPT OF LEAVING THE WORK
questionText: A and B can do a work in 15 days and 30 days, respectively. They start working together, but A leaves after 3 days. How much time will B take to complete the remaining work?
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(15, 30) = 30\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of A} = 2,\quad \text{Efficiency of B} = 1$$
$$\text{Work done by (A + B) in 3 days} = 3 \times (2 + 1) = 9\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 30 - 9 = 21\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by B alone} = \frac{21}{1} = 21\text{ days}$$

typeHeader: TYPE - IV: CONCEPT OF LEAVING THE WORK
questionText: Raja and Rocky together can complete painting work in 5 days. Together they both start painting, but after 2 days, Rocky falls sick and leaves the work. If Raja completes the remaining painting in 4 days, find the number of days in which Rocky alone can do the work.
solution:
$$\text{Work done by (Raja + Rocky) in 2 days} = \frac{2}{5}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 1 - \frac{2}{5} = \frac{3}{5}$$
$$\text{Rate of Raja} = \frac{3/5}{4} = \frac{3}{20}\text{ work/day}$$
$$\text{Combined rate} = \frac{1}{5} = \frac{4}{20}\text{ work/day}$$
$$\text{Rate of Rocky} = \frac{4}{20} - \frac{3}{20} = \frac{1}{20}\text{ work/day}$$
$$\text{Time taken by Rocky alone} = 20\text{ days}$$

typeHeader: TYPE - IV: CONCEPT OF LEAVING THE WORK
questionText: A and B can complete a work in 36 days and 45 days respectively. They worked together for 2 days and then A left the work. In how many days will B complete the remaining work?
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(36, 45) = 180\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of A} = 5,\quad \text{Efficiency of B} = 4$$
$$\text{Work done by (A + B) in 2 days} = 2 \times (5 + 4) = 18\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 180 - 18 = 162\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by B alone} = \frac{162}{4} = 40.5\text{ days}$$

typeHeader: TYPE - IV: CONCEPT OF LEAVING THE WORK
questionText: X can complete half of the work in 20 days and Y can do one-fifth of the same work in 10 days. X started the work and left after 8 days. Then Y took over to complete the remaining work. The total number of days taken by them to complete the work is:
solution:
$$\text{Time for X to complete whole work} = 20 \times 2 = 40\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Time for Y to complete whole work} = 10 \times 5 = 50\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(40, 50) = 200\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of X} = 5,\quad \text{Efficiency of Y} = 4$$
$$\text{Work done by X in 8 days} = 8 \times 5 = 40\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 200 - 40 = 160\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by Y alone} = \frac{160}{4} = 40\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Total days taken by them} = 8 + 40 = 48\text{ days}$$

typeHeader: TYPE - IV: CONCEPT OF LEAVING THE WORK
questionText: B and C can complete a work alone in 10 days and 30 days respectively. They began the work together but B left the work after some days and C completed the remaining work in 10 days. After how many days from the beginning B left the work?
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(10, 30) = 30\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of B} = 3,\quad \text{Efficiency of C} = 1$$
$$\text{Work done by C alone in last 10 days} = 10 \times 1 = 10\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work done by (B + C)} = 30 - 10 = 20\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Combined efficiency of B and C} = 3 + 1 = 4\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Days B and C worked together} = \frac{20}{4} = 5\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Hence, B left after 5 days from the beginning.}$$

typeHeader: TYPE - IV: CONCEPT OF LEAVING THE WORK
questionText: A can complete work in 25 days and B can complete the same work in 20 days. They started the work together but B left after 4 days and A continued to work. In how many days will the entire work be completed?
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(25, 20) = 100\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of A} = 4,\quad \text{Efficiency of B} = 5$$
$$\text{Work done by (A + B) in 4 days} = 4 \times (4 + 5) = 36\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 100 - 36 = 64\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by A alone} = \frac{64}{4} = 16\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Total days to complete entire work} = 4 + 16 = 20\text{ days}$$

typeHeader: TYPE - IV: CONCEPT OF LEAVING THE WORK
questionText: A, B and C can individually complete a work in 24, 15 and 12 days respectively. B and C started the work and left after working for 3 days, how many days will A take to complete the remaining work?
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(24, 15, 12) = 120\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of A} = 5,\quad \text{Efficiency of B} = 8,\quad \text{Efficiency of C} = 10$$
$$\text{Work done by (B + C) in 3 days} = 3 \times (8 + 10) = 54\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 120 - 54 = 66\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by A alone} = \frac{66}{5} = 13\frac{1}{5}\text{ days}$$

typeHeader: TYPE - IV: CONCEPT OF LEAVING THE WORK
questionText: Shivam can do a piece of work in 6 days and Vivek in 24 days. They started work together but Shivam left the work 3 days before its completion. In how many days was the work completed?
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(6, 24) = 24\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of Shivam} = 4,\quad \text{Efficiency of Vivek} = 1$$
$$\text{Work done by Vivek alone in last 3 days} = 3 \times 1 = 3\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Work done together by Shivam and Vivek} = 24 - 3 = 21\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Days worked together} = \frac{21}{4 + 1} = \frac{21}{5} = 4\frac{1}{5}\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Total days to complete the work} = 4\frac{1}{5} + 3 = 7\frac{1}{5}\text{ days}$$

typeHeader: TYPE - IV: CONCEPT OF LEAVING THE WORK
questionText: A and B can individually complete a piece of work in 18 days and 30 days, respectively. A and B started working together, but A left $16\frac{2}{3}$ days before the work is completed and B alone completed the rest of the work. For how many days did A work?
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(18, 30) = 90\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of A} = 5,\quad \text{Efficiency of B} = 3$$
$$16\frac{2}{3}\text{ days} = \frac{50}{3}\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Work done by B alone in the last } \frac{50}{3}\text{ days} = \frac{50}{3} \times 3 = 50\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work done by (A + B) together} = 90 - 50 = 40\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Combined efficiency of (A + B)} = 5 + 3 = 8\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Days A and B worked together} = \frac{40}{8} = 5\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Therefore, A worked for 5 days.}$$
